post.summary: `POST /api/auth/oidc/backchannel-logout` — OIDC Back-Channel Logout 1.0.
post.description:
Keycloak (or any conformant IdP) calls this server-to-server when a user logs
out or their session ends upstream. There is no cookie and no CSRF token on
this request — it's secured entirely by the logout token's JWS signature
(verified against the provider's JWKS, `iss`/`aud`/`exp` enforced) — see
[`crate::oidc::verify_logout_token`]. On success, every egret session for the
token's `sub` is revoked. An unrecognized `sub` (e.g. a user who never
completed OIDC login) is a no-op 200, matching the spec's guidance that the
RP should not leak whether it knows a given subject. Always sets
`Cache-Control: no-store` per the Back-Channel Logout spec.

200.description: Logout token accepted; matching sessions (if any) revoked

400.description: Missing/invalid logout token, or JWKS unavailable

parameters.description: Authorization code from the OIDC provider

post.summary:
`POST /engines/{id}/catalogs/{cid}/test` — "test connection": runs
`SHOW SCHEMAS FROM "<catalog>"` against the engine's Trino coordinator via
the native-monitor coordinator proxy ([`crate::monitor::coordinator_call`],

coordinator-proxied routes in this file and in `monitor.rs`).

post.summary: Restore an earlier revision by replaying it through the ordinary update path.
post.description:
The snapshot CARRIES the card and tab ids it was taken with, so a revert keeps the id of every
card that still exists instead of renumbering the whole dashboard. Nothing is remapped here:
`replace_layout` decides what an id means, and it honours one only when this dashboard already
owns it — a card deleted since the revision comes back with a fresh id, and an id that never
belonged here cannot be adopted. (This is still NOT `DashboardRepo::duplicate`, which needs a
tab_map because it copies rows into a DIFFERENT dashboard.)

A revision recorded before ids were carried has none, and reverts exactly as it always did —
every card inserted fresh. Revalidation is
not optional: a chart a revision references may have been deleted since, and
`require_cards_in_ws` inside `apply_dashboard_update` turns that into a 404 rather than a
dangling card.

The revert is itself recorded, as kind 'revert', so undoing a revert is an ordinary revert.

`POST /api/ws/{workspace}/impersonate` — a `ws_admin` of `{workspace}` (or a
platform_admin) starts impersonating a MEMBER of that workspace. The resulting

Guards run in a deliberate order so a caller learns nothing before its own
authority is proven: (1) not already impersonating; (2) caller is `ws_admin`

then mirrors the platform endpoint: a local caller re-enters their password; an
OIDC caller gets a `409` with an authorize URL whose sealed intent carries this
`workspace_id`, and the overlay is created by the OIDC callback.

CardInput.description: Card as supplied by the client when saving a layout.

id.description:
The id this card already has, so a save can UPDATE it instead of replacing it.

Absent means "new card" — which is what every client sent before this field existed, and
what a card the user has just dropped onto the canvas still sends. It is a HINT, not an
instruction: the server keeps the id only when it already belongs to THIS dashboard (see
`replace_layout`), so a stale or borrowed id can never make one dashboard adopt another's
card.

`skip_serializing_if` keeps a body without ids byte-identical to what it was before this
field existed — `update_dashboard_round_trips_through_json_unchanged` caught the `"id":
null` this would otherwise have added to every card of every re-serialized body.

CardRunBody.description:
Optional body for the card-data endpoint: resolved dashboard-parameter filters
to merge into the card chart's persisted query. Reuses `chartquery::Filter`
(the same `{ col, op, value }` shape the chart spec uses), so the frontend
sends exactly what `applyParamsToChart` produces. Each filter's `col` is
validated against the dataset's real columns before it is applied (an unknown
column → 400), and the values/operators are rendered through the same
injection-safe `sql_literal`/`FilterOp` path as the persisted filters.

filters.description: Resolved, dashboard-param-derived filters to AND onto the card's saved query.

temporal_units.description:
Resolved `temporal_unit` dashboard-param overrides: dimension column name ->
temporal unit token (e.g. "month"). Each token is validated against the
`TemporalUnit` enum by `chartquery::build` (an unknown token → 400) and rendered
as an enum-driven bucket expression — never spliced into SQL as a raw string.
A client override replaces the saved unit for that already-gridded column.

ChartDataBody.description:
Build-only data request: produce SQL for a dataset + QuerySpec; the client submits it
to the existing /queries endpoint and polls.

Stays in `egret-bi` (not the leaf contract crate): its `query_spec` field is the
`egret-bi`-local [`QuerySpec`] query builder, which references `egret-query-api`
and other in-crate types and so cannot move to the leaf.

ChartRunResponse.description:
A saved chart's query, executed: columns + row-major rows. Mirrors the first
two fields of `TabularResult` so the frontend consumes it like a query
result. Returned by the object-scoped `POST /charts/{id}/data` endpoint,
which runs ONLY the chart's persisted query (no client-supplied spec).

rows.description: Row-major cell values; each inner vec is one row aligned to `columns`.

ColumnMeta.description: One column's name + engine-reported type name.

ColumnSpec.description:
The frozen form of a `ColumnMeta`. Deliberately its own type rather than
re-using `egret_core::ColumnMeta`: this one is persisted inside a published
snapshot, so it must stay stable even if the engine-facing type gains or
renames a field.

impersonate.description:
Run each query as the logged-in user (impersonate delegation mode).
Trino → `X-Trino-User`; StarRocks → `EXECUTE AS <user> WITH NO REVERT`.
Requires engine impersonation + Ranger. Default false.

tls_cert.description:
PEM of the engine's self-signed cert to pin as a trusted root (server-auth
over TLS). Set on egret-provisioned TLS connections — Trino jwt/TLS mode
(https) and StarRocks delegation (in-band TLS on :9030).

CreateEndpointInput.description:
The `POST` body.

The spec fields are `Option<T>` rather than `#[serde(default)] T` because
`CacheSpec`/`LimitsSpec`/`RateLimitSpec` deliberately have no `Default` impl —
`OutputSpec`'s hand-written one exists precisely because a derive would have
diverged from serde's defaults. An absent field is stored as `'{}'::jsonb` and
read back through the same serde defaults, so there is exactly one definition
of "the default" and no Rust-side copy of it to drift.
`deny_unknown_fields`: a misspelled TOP-LEVEL key is a 400 naming the field,
not a silently discarded value. Every field here is either required or
`#[serde(default)]`, so nothing legitimate is refused.

This attribute covers only this struct's own keys — it does not reach a
nested one. The nested config types carry their own; see the note above
`ParamSpec` in `egret-dataapi-api`, which is where the reported case
(`{"rate_limit": {"per_client_qps": 5}}` returning 201 with the limit
defaulted to `0`) is actually refused. Both layers are needed.

path.description:
Free-form and user-typed. **Total-reject, not normalised**: a leading
slash is optional and one trailing slash is absorbed, but anything else
out of shape — an empty segment, a `.`/`..` segment, percent-encoding, a
query string, a fragment, whitespace, a character outside
`[A-Za-z0-9._~-]`, or a value over [`MAX_PATH_LEN`] bytes — is a 400
naming the reason. Nothing is silently rewritten. See [`normalize_path`].

database_id.description:
The connection this endpoint queries. Validated against the CALLER's
workspace by the route before it is stored — it arrives from the request
body, so nothing else would stop it naming another workspace's database.

trinoConfig.description:
Optional full per-role config surface, stored under `spec["trinoConfig"]`.
Wire shape: `{ queryMaxMemory, logLevel, configProperties, env,
coordinator{replicas, resources, heap, queryMaxMemoryPerNode,
additionalJvmConfig, probes}, worker{... , gracefulShutdown} }`. On create
the simple wizard fields seed this; `update` sends the full per-role block.

authzServiceId.description:
Link the new engine to an EXISTING Ranger profile (authz_services id).
When omitted, provisioning creates a fresh profile named after the engine.

kind.description:
Which engine to provision: `"trino"` (default, back-compat) or
`"starrocks"`. Selects between the Trino spec-building path and
[`create_starrocks_engine`].

oneOf.description:
StarRocks-specific config surface (FE/CN image + replicas + optional
resources); only read when `kind == "starrocks"`. Storage (endpoint/
path/keys) is NOT accepted here — it's derived from the warehouse's
storage connection, same as the Trino S3 connector.

tlsCertSecretRef.description: Optional: a kubernetes.io/tls named secret to back the coordinator TLS.

config.description: Optional service config (e.g. StarRocks JDBC coordinates). Stored verbatim.

CreateSchedule.description:
Create body. `type` decides which optional block is required, checked in the
route before the database's CHECK constraints see it, so the client gets a
message naming the missing field rather than a constraint name.

message.description:
A user-authored note carried into the notification body. Distinct from
`description`, which is the line the LIST shows.

message_footer.description:
The closing note, rendered UNDER the result — `message` opens the
notification, this one closes it, and an inline image sits between them.
Defaulted, so a client written before 0116 keeps working unchanged.

skip_if_empty.description: Metabase's `skip_if_empty`: send nothing when the run produced no rows.

targets.description:
Objects a REPORT delivers, in page order. Empty falls back to the
single `chart_id`/`dashboard_id`, which is every pre-0115 row.

owners.description:
Owner user ids. Empty means "the creator", resolved server-side — a
schedule with no owner has no identity to run as (§5.2).

CreateSecretInput.description:
Request body for creating a global named secret. Either a typed `data` map
(with `type`, default `Opaque`) or the legacy single `value` (→ Opaque{value}).

value.description: Back-compat: a single value stored as `Opaque{value}`.

Display name for `created_by` — the profile name, else the email. Resolved server-side:
the endpoints that can turn a user id into a name are admin-gated, so the browser cannot
do it for an ordinary workspace editor. Same shape and same reason as
`MemberDto.principal_name`.

created_at.description: NULL for dashboards predating migration 0106, which does not invent a creation date.

updated_by_name.description: Display name for `updated_by`, resolved the same way as `created_by_name`.

folder_id.description:
The folder this dashboard is filed under; NULL = Uncategorized. Present on
`DashboardSummaryDto` since folders shipped, and absent here until now, which is why the
info sidebar had no folder to name.

certified.description:
Marked as trusted by a steward. Same three fields datasets and metrics have carried since
0098, so "is this certified" is one question across the product rather than three.

certified_by.description:
Who certified it, as their email — the string is read by whoever sees the badge, and a
uuid would tell them nothing. Empty while `certified` is false.

certification_details.description:
Why, in the certifier's words. Empty is allowed: a certification with no note is still a
certification.

can_manage.description:
May the CALLER edit this dashboard? Workspace-scoped `dashboard:manage`, answered by the
PDP — the session's permission list carries platform grants only and can never contain it.

DashboardRevisionDto.description:
One entry in a dashboard's History tab.

The `snapshot` is deliberately NOT on this DTO. A 22-card dashboard's PUT body is hundreds of
kilobytes and the cap is twenty of them, so shipping the content would make opening the info
sidebar a multi-megabyte download for a list the user reads as six lines of text. Revert takes
a revision id and does the work server-side, where the snapshot already is.

created_by_name.description:
Display name for `created_by`, resolved server-side for the same reason
`DashboardDetailDto.created_by_name` is.

is_current.description:
True for the revision that matches the dashboard's live state — the newest one. The client
suppresses the revert action on it rather than deriving "newest" from the array order,
which would silently become wrong the day the endpoint gains a sort parameter.

certified.description:
A steward has vouched for this dashboard. Display only — the list carries no
`certified_by`, since the badge here answers "is it trusted", and "by whom" is a
question the detail page already answers.

can_manage.description:
Whether this caller may run the list's mutating actions — duplicate, move, trash,
delete.

WORKSPACE-SCOPED, AND THE SAME ON EVERY ROW. Unlike `DashboardDetailDto.can_manage`,
which is evaluated against the individual object, this is one workspace-level decision
copied across the response. That is deliberate: a per-object answer costs two SQL
queries PER ROW (`grants_for` plus the classification-tag lookup inside `CedarPdp`),
so a 100-dashboard list would issue 200 extra queries to draw a menu.

The cost of the shortcut is a FALSE NEGATIVE, never a false positive: someone who holds
manage only through a per-object or per-folder share sees the row menu withheld here.
They lose nothing they cannot recover — opening the dashboard runs the real per-object
check and gives them the editor. The opposite error, offering Trash to a reader, is the
one that costs.

DataApiClientDto.description:
What a client list returns. There is deliberately NO secret field — not a
skipped one, not an `Option`. A field that cannot exist cannot leak through a
future serde attribute change.

Named with the `DataApi` prefix because utoipa keys components by Rust type
name and those names are GLOBAL after `openapi_doc()` merges the seams —
`egret-catalog-engine` already publishes a `ClientDto`, and a collision
silently overwrites one of them in the merged document.

DataApiEndpointDto.description:
An endpoint draft as the management UI sees it.

Named with the `DataApi` prefix for the same reason `DataApiClientDto` is:
utoipa keys components by Rust type name and those names are GLOBAL once
`openapi_doc()` merges the seams, so a bare `EndpointDto` is a collision
waiting for the next seam that wants the word.

live_version_id.description:
The version currently served. Never written by this module — publishing
is a separate lifecycle.

DataApiEndpointVersionDto.description: A published version, as the API reports it.

is_live.description: True for the version `endpoints.live_version_id` points at.

snapshot.description:
The frozen definition. **This is the only thing P4 may read to decide what
a request returns** — see the module comment.

DataApiNewClientDto.description: The issue response, and the only type in the crate carrying secret material.

token_endpoint.description: Where to exchange these for a token.

DataApiPublishedDto.description: What `publish`/`rollback` report back about the version now being served.

DataApiServiceAccountDto.description:
A service account as the management UI sees it. `id` is the `users.id` — a
service account is a real user row, so this is the id that appears in
`access_grants`, Cedar and audit.

email.description: The synthetic address `users.email` requires. Not a mailbox.

columns.description:
The output schema `describe` resolved. This is what `publish` would
freeze, so an author sees the contract before committing to it.

Database.description:
A full database registration row (no secret material).

`Serialize`/`Deserialize` are forward-looking contract surface: today the
wire type is the separate `DatabaseDetailDto` and the store builds `Database`
field-by-field from sqlx rows, so these codecs are not yet exercised — they
let a future out-of-process query-seam client exchange this domain type.

delegated.description: B3a: run BI queries as the caller's per-user engine JWT (delegation).

engine_id.description:
Set when this row was materialized by an engine→workspace assignment.
A non-null `engine_id` marks the connection provisioned (read-only,
per-user-delegated) and links it back to the source engine.

Set (as a UUID string) when this connection was materialized by an
engine→workspace assignment (read-only, provisioned by egret); `None`
for a self-service connection. The frontend uses it to split the
workspace Engines page into provisioned vs. self-service groups.

DatabaseInput.description:
Register/update body. Credentials are a NAMED secret (Epic B): either
`new_secret` (mint a new named secret inline) or `secret_id` (reference an
existing named secret in the workspace). Omitting both registers a connection
with no secret (or, on update, keeps the existing one).

delegated.description: B3a: run BI queries as the caller's per-user engine JWT (delegation).

DatabaseListDto.description: Minimal listing for the Explorer DB picker (no connection internals).

groupby.description: Usable as a groupby dimension in charts.

filterable.description: Usable as a filter in charts.

semantic_type.description: Semantic role driving smart rendering and chart defaults; "" = none. Rejected with 400 if not one of the listed values.

DatasetDataBody.description:
Body of the object-scoped dataset data-preview: an OPTIONAL row cap only.
There is deliberately NO client SQL field — the endpoint always runs
`SELECT * FROM <the dataset's own source>`, so a shared reader can preview
only the dataset its grant covers. Unknown fields are ignored.

limit.description: Rows to preview. Clamped to [100, 1000]; defaults to 200 when absent.

certified.description: Certified as a trusted/official dataset (for a list badge).

DatasetUsageDto.description: A chart that uses a dataset (for the dataset Usage view).

seconds.description: Soft-delete retention in seconds; null = hard delete.

note.description: Optional note recorded on the denied request.

DiscoveryDoc.description:
OIDC discovery document served at `/.well-known/openid-configuration` so the
embedded lakekeeper can locate this IdP's JWKS + token endpoint. Doc-only
mirror of the `serde_json::Value` the handler builds.

EndpointSnapshot.description:
What a published version freezes. Self-contained on purpose: P4's serving
path must be able to answer a request from this alone, without reading the
draft row.

delegated.description:
Whether `database_id` delegated per-user credentials to the engine at the
moment this version was published.

**The one input to the frozen contract that lives outside the snapshot.**
`query.databases.delegated` is a mutable column: `cache.scope = shared` is
refused at publish time on a delegated connection (Ranger filters rows per
principal, so a shared cache serves one caller's rows to another), but a
non-delegated connection can be flipped to delegated afterwards, and no
re-validation runs anywhere when it is. Freezing the value publish
validated against is what lets the serving path notice.

**P4 must compare this against the live `delegated` before serving from a
shared cache, and refuse when they disagree.** Every other field here is
self-contained; this one is a witness, and it is only useful if it is
checked.

columns.description:
Resolved by `describe_as` at publish time and frozen here, so the
published contract does not drift when the underlying table changes.

EngineCatalogDetailDto.description:
`GET /engines/{id}/catalogs/{cid}` payload: full stored config + secretRef,
with system-minted secret material redacted (see [`redact_catalog_config`]).

EngineDetailDto.description: `GET /engines/{id}` payload: the engine row flattened with live status.

EngineOption.description: An engine (DB connection) option shown in notebook settings.

enabled.description: Whether this engine is currently enabled for notebooks in this workspace.

EngineSpecDto.description:
The provisioning parameters surfaced back to clients (subset of the stored
`spec` jsonb; internal bookkeeping keys are ignored on deserialize).

trinoConfig.description: Surfaced back so the UI can prefill the config editor on reload.

starrocksConfig.description:
StarRocks equivalent of `trino_config`: the persisted `starrocksConfig`
block (images/replicas/resources/delegation/feConfig/cnConfig/
cnAutoscaling/pod) surfaced back so the UI can prefill the StarRocks
config editor + show KPIs/auth on reload. Absent for Trino engines.

tls_cert.description:
The engine's self-signed TLS cert (PEM) when it serves over TLS, so the
kernel can PIN it (verify against this cert only) instead of disabling
verification. `None` for plain-HTTP engines.

EngineWorkspaceDto.description: A workspace an engine is assigned to (CP `…/workspaces` list payload).

ErrorBody.description:
The JSON body every error response carries: `{ "error": "<message>" }`.

This is the OpenAPI schema counterpart of the body produced by
`IntoResponse for Error` above — the single shape returned for every 4xx/5xx
across the API. Handlers reference it in their `#[utoipa::path]`
`responses(...)` for the error statuses. 5xx messages are redacted to
`"internal error"`; client-facing errors pass their `Display` message.

code.description:
Machine-readable discriminant, present only where clients must branch on
the reason. Currently only `"feature_disabled"`. Omitted otherwise, so
no existing response changes shape.

FeatureDto.description: One module and whether this workspace has it switched on.

value.description:
Comparison operand. Scalar for most operators; a JSON array for `in`/`not_in`;
ignored for `is_null`/`is_not_null`. Validated against the column's generic type.

ImpersonationDto.description:
The active impersonation as surfaced by `/me`: who is being acted-as
(`target`), the admin behind it (`impersonator`), and the overlay's bounds.

expires_at.description: Optional hard expiry. Absent means the client lives until revoked.

JoinableWorkspaceDto.description: A workspace a user may request to join (they are not already a member).

JwksDoc.description:
JWK set served at `/.well-known/jwks.json`. Doc-only mirror of the
`serde_json::Value` the handler builds; each key is a raw RFC 7517 JWK.

KernelStatus.description:
Public snapshot of a kernel: phase + gateway URL.

Serializes as `{ "phase": "ready", "url": "http://..." }`.

phase.description:
Lifecycle phase, serialized as a lowercase string
(`spawning` / `ready` / `dead`).

oneOf.description:
Present when the caller is currently impersonating another user (an active
admin overlay resolved to the target). `null` for an ordinary session.

NewSecret.description:
Request shape for creating a brand-new named secret inline while registering a
connection (storage or database): `{ "name": ..., "value": ... }`. The value
is plaintext, accepted only on write and never returned. Shared across the
HTTP layers so each connection type can mint a named secret in one request.

value.description: Plaintext secret value; accepted only on write, never returned.

id.description:
The id this tab already has. Same contract as [`CardInput::id`]: a hint, honoured only when
the tab already belongs to this dashboard.

Tabs need it for a reason cards do not: `dashboard_cards.tab_id` is `ON DELETE CASCADE`, so
recreating a tab took every card on it with it — the cards were being deleted twice over.

NotebookRuntime.description:
Full kernel manifest returned by `GET /ws/{workspace}/notebook-runtime` and
consumed by `egret-kernel` to build the kernel process environment.

username.description: The caller's stable username (email local-part, collision-suffixed).

engines.description: Workspace engines (DB connections) enabled for notebooks.

engine_jwt.description:
Short-lived per-user engine JWT the kernel presents to query engines.
`None` when the caller has no stored refresh token (e.g. password/local
users or OIDC logins without an offline token) — minting is best-effort
since no P1 engine consumes this yet.

engine_jwt_expires_at.description:
Expiry of `engine_jwt` (RFC3339); kernels re-mint before this time.
`None` whenever `engine_jwt` is `None`.

catalog_jwt.description:
Short-lived `aud:"catalog"` JWT scoped to the workspace's notebook
warehouse — the kernel presents it to the Iceberg REST catalog for
direct notebook writes. `None` when no notebook warehouse is configured
or minting failed (best-effort; the kernel helper errors at call time).

catalog_uri.description:
Base URI of the Iceberg REST catalog the kernel writes to
(`<catalog_base_url>/catalog`). `None` when no warehouse is configured.

catalog_warehouse.description:
Lakekeeper warehouse id the `catalog_jwt` is scoped to. `None` when no
warehouse is configured.

namespace.description:
Private namespace path notebook writes land under (e.g. `["notebook"]`).
Empty when no warehouse is configured.

NotebookSetFolder.description:
Body for `PATCH /notebooks/{id}/folder`: move a notebook into a folder
(or back to Uncategorized with `folder_id: null`).

Renamed in the OpenAPI doc to `NotebookSetFolder` to avoid a global schema
collision with `egret_analytics_api::bi::SetFolder` (the BI seam's identically
named body); the wire shape is unchanged.

warehouse_id.description: The workspace's chosen notebook (scratch) Iceberg warehouse, if set.

namespace.description: The private namespace path notebook writes land under (empty when unset).

NotebookSummary.description: Summary view of a notebook (no cells). Used by ownership/IDOR gates.

bookmarked.description: Whether the requesting viewer has bookmarked this notebook.

folder_id.description: Folder this notebook lives in; `None` = Uncategorized.

ObjectGrantBody.description: Body of a share grant: give `principal` a workspace `role` on this object.

principal_id.description: A user's email, a group's name, or a UUID.

role.description:
`ws_viewer` (Viewer, read) | `ws_editor` (Editor, manage). For a "Blocked"
grant, send `ws_editor` with `effect="deny"`.

effect.description: `allow` (default) | `deny`. A deny blocks the principal on this object.

expires_at.description:
Optional expiry (RFC3339). `None` = never expires (unchanged default).
Enforced at read time by the PDP/admission predicates, not here.

ObjectGrantDto.description: A single object-scoped grant on the object.

principal_name.description:
Human-readable grantee name: a user's email or a group's name. `None` if
the principal row could not be resolved (e.g. deleted).

expires_at.description:
Optional expiry (P2a). `None` = never expires. This is the object's own
direct-grant list (manage-only), so an expired grant is still listed
here — only the read-time admission predicates exclude expired grants.

Optional expiry (RFC3339). `None` = never expires. This is the
management roll-up, so an expired grant is still returned (not filtered).

OidcStepUp.description:
`409` body returned when an OIDC-provider admin starts an impersonation: the
client must redirect the browser to `authorize_url` to complete a fresh IdP
re-authentication (`prompt=login`) before the overlay is created (Task 8). The
`code` lets the SPA branch on this specific response.

authorize_url.description: The OIDC authorize URL (carries the sealed impersonation intent in `state`).

OwnerDto.description:
A schedule owner. The owner is a security-relevant field, not decoration:
the alert's query runs with this user's permissions at run time (§5.2).

ParamSpec.description:
`deny_unknown_fields` on the author-supplied config types.

`#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` on the request-body struct does NOT reach a
nested one, and the nested one is where the damage was: posting the
documented-but-wrong `{"rate_limit": {"per_client_qps": 5}}` returned 201
with `per_key_qps` silently defaulted to `0`. A rate limit the author
believes they set and did not is worse than an error.

Applied to the five types an AUTHOR fills in — [`ParamSpec`], [`CacheSpec`],
[`LimitsSpec`], [`RateLimitSpec`], [`OutputSpec`] — and deliberately NOT to
[`EndpointSnapshot`] or [`ColumnSpec`], which the server writes for itself
and where a typo is impossible.

**The cost, stated because it is a real constraint on a persisted format.**
These types are also how a stored `jsonb` column is read back. Adding a field
in some future version and then rolling the binary back would make the older
code refuse to deserialize rows the newer one wrote, as a 500 on read. That is
a loud failure rather than a silent one, and it is the standard price of
strict deserialization; a future field that must be readable by older code has
to be introduced some other way.

allowed.description:
Required when `ty` is `Enum`. The ONLY safe form for anything that
reaches an identifier position — see spec §3.

PolicySummary.description: Flattened, UI-facing view of one stored Ranger policy.

Principal.description: One egret identity offered by the policy picker.

name.description: The value written into the policy (user email / group name).

ProfileDto.description: A profile (Ranger service) + the engine(s) that link to it.

tag_service.description:
The classification-tag policy service this Trino profile carries its
tag-based masking/row-filters in (the configured `tagService` or the
`<name>_tag` convention), if such a service exists. `None` otherwise — the
FE shows a "Tags" tab only when this is set.

PublishEndpointInput.description: The `POST /publish` body. Every field optional, so `{}` is a valid publish.

note.description: Free-form "what changed", stored on the version.

QueryParam.description:
A single SQL-Lab template parameter. `value` is substituted for `{{name}}`
as a typed, escaped SQL literal (never raw text) so parameters cannot inject.

temporal_units.description:
dimension column name -> temporal unit token (snake_case, e.g. "month", "day_of_week").
Empty (default) = no truncation = legacy behavior.

QueryStatusDto.description: Full status view (preview inline; full result via the results endpoint).

columns.description: Column metadata `[{name,type}]`; `null` until the query finishes.

preview.description: Inline preview rows (bounded, row-major); `null` until the query finishes.

RangerErrorBody.description:
Doc-only mirror of the Ranger error envelope (`{ msg, statusCode }`), which
differs from the control-plane `ErrorBody` shape.

RangerServiceDefs.description: Doc-only mirror of the `{ "serviceDefs": [...] }` envelope `list_defs` returns.

serviceDefs.description: Each element is a raw Ranger service-definition object (stored verbatim).

RangerServicePolicies.description:
Doc-only mirror of the `ServicePolicies` plugin download envelope
(`egret-policy-api`) returned by `download_policies`.

policies.description: The service's enabled policies, each a raw Ranger policy object.

RangerServiceTags.description: Doc-only mirror of the empty `ServiceTags` payload returned by `download_tags`.

tags.description: Tag map keyed by numeric tag-id → tag-def instance.

resourceToTagIds.description: `{ "<resourceId>": [<tagId>, ...] }` linking each resource to its tags.

RecipientDto.description:
A delivery destination. `config` is kind-dependent — `{"addresses": [...]}`
for email, `{"url": "...", "secret_id": "..."}` for webhook — and is
validated against `kind` on the way in.

RecipientInput.description: A recipient as submitted; the id is assigned by the server.

RecipientKind.description: Where a firing schedule delivers to.

RenderCard.description:
One card's IDENTITY and query shape — no rows.

Step one of the render. The page needs the saved spec to resolve the
dashboard's parameters against it, which it cannot do if the server has
already run the query.

param_mappings.description:
`dashboard_cards.options.paramMappings`: parameter id -> the column on
THIS card it filters. A parameter with no mapping here does not apply to
this card, which is why the mapping travels per card rather than once
for the dashboard.

RenderCardData.description: One card's DATA. Step two, once the page has resolved the filters.

RenderCardRequest.description:
What the page asks for in step two: the resolved dashboard-parameter
filters for one card.

The same shape as `egret_bi`'s `CardRunBody`, and merged the same way —
onto the card's SAVED spec, never replacing it. A client supplies FILTERS,
never a query: each `col` is checked against the dataset's real columns by
`compile_chart_sql` -> `chartquery::build` -> `find_column`, and each
temporal unit against the `TemporalUnit` enum. Accepting a whole spec here
would let whoever holds a render token run arbitrary SQL as the schedule's
owner.

parameters.description:
The dashboard's parameter definitions, verbatim. The print page resolves
them to filters with `applyParamsToChart` — the SAME module the
interactive dashboard uses — and sends the result back to
[`run_cards`].

Ported to Rust instead, this would be a second implementation of six
text operators, relative date windows and month/quarter/year arithmetic
that must agree with the first one exactly, forever. When they drifted,
the emailed image would quietly stop matching the dashboard — which is
the bug this whole path exists to fix.

`null` for a chart report: a chart has no parameters.

ResourceTagBody.description:
Body of an assign/unassign: the resource (`column` optional ⇒ table-level) +
the tag id.

ResourceTagDto.description:
A catalog resource tag on the wire (snake_case). `column` is empty for a
table-level tag. The tag itself is nested under `tag` (the full P3.1 tag
shape, matching the FE `Tag` type) so the browse UI can read `a.tag`.

ResultsPage.description: A page of the full result.

rows.description: Row-major cell values; each element is one row (a JSON array).

parentRoleId.description:
The role this one inherits permissions from (same scope). `None` at the
top of a chain.

inheritedPermissions.description:
Effective-minus-own permissions, for read-only display. Populated on the
single-role GET; empty on the list endpoint.

RollbackEndpointInput.description:
The `POST /rollback` body: name the version by NUMBER or by ID, not both.

`version` is scoped to the endpoint by construction — version numbers are only
unique within one endpoint's history — so that spelling cannot name another
endpoint's version even in principle. `version_id` is a bare uuid and
therefore CAN, which is precisely why the store's statement carries
`v.endpoint_id = e.id`. Both exist because a UI listing versions has their ids
to hand while a human types a number.

RunDto.description: One entry in the run-log drawer.

RunState.description:
Superset's five run states, verbatim. They are the vocabulary that makes the
list page legible — in particular `noop` ("ran, condition false") and `grace`
("would have fired, suppressed") are the two answers to "why didn't I get an
email?", and collapsing either into `success` loses that answer.

folder_id.description: Folder this saved query lives in (`None` = root). Serialized as a string.

ScheduleDetailDto.description:
The editor's view: everything on the summary plus the type-specific blocks,
recipients, and the advanced knobs.

message.description:
A user-authored note carried into the notification body. Distinct from
`description`, which is the line the LIST shows.

message_footer.description:
The closing note, rendered UNDER the result — `message` opens the
notification, this one closes it, and an inline image sits between them.
Defaulted, so a client written before 0116 keeps working unchanged.

skip_if_empty.description: Metabase's `skip_if_empty`: send nothing when the run produced no rows.

targets.description:
Objects a REPORT delivers, in page order. Empty falls back to the
single `chart_id`/`dashboard_id`, which is every pre-0115 row.

ScheduleSummaryDto.description:
One row of the list page.

`last_state` is the column the page exists for, so it is on the summary
rather than the detail — a list that needs a second request per row to say
whether anything is broken would not be opened.

can_manage.description:
Whether the caller may edit/delete schedules in this workspace.

One workspace-level answer repeated on every row, not a per-object
decision — `alert:manage` is workspace-scoped, so the answer is the same
for the whole list. It exists because the client CANNOT derive it: a
session's `permissions` carries PLATFORM grants only, so a UI that
guessed would show a reader destructive controls that 403 on click.

bookmarked.description: Whether the CALLER has starred this one — per-user, unlike `can_manage`.

folder_id.description: The folder this row is grouped under, or `None` for "Uncategorized".

deleted_at.description: Set only in the trash view; `None` for a live schedule.

ScheduleType.description:
What a schedule does: evaluate a query (`alert`) or deliver a rendering of a
saved object (`report`).

SchemaColumn.description: A single column in a DESCRIBE result.

SearchHit.description:
A schema-object search hit (a table/view matched by the SQL Lab global
object search). `catalog` is empty for engines without a catalog level.

SecretDto.description: Response DTO mirroring `WorkspaceSecretMeta` (never exposes the plaintext).

SeedResult.description: Doc-only mirror of the `{ "created": <n> }` body `seed_defaults` returns.

created.description: How many default policies were created (0 if the profile already had any).

columns.description:
The FROZEN columns from the snapshot, not the ones this execution
happened to return. The published contract is what a client codes
against; if the underlying table has drifted, the difference is a defect
to surface, not something to paper over by reporting today's shape.

ServingResponse.description:
The success body (spec §5.1.2).

`meta.version` is the published version that served the call, so a
client-side bug is reproducible against the exact snapshot that produced it.
`meta.cached` is likewise not cosmetic: without it a stale-looking result is
indistinguishable from a fresh one while debugging. It is hard-`false` until
Task 4 lands the cache — a field that lies would be worse than no field.

data.description:
Rows, shaped by the snapshot's `output.shape`: an array of objects
(default) or an array of arrays.

required_roles.description:
Clearance role NAMES; a principal needs `>= 1` to access objects carrying
this tag. Cleared = `>= 1` role OR `>= 1` group; both empty = no gate.

required_groups.description:
Clearance GROUP ids (as strings; Access P3.4). Each is parsed as a `Uuid`
before hitting the repo — a non-uuid entry is rejected `400 BadRequest`
(never spliced unvalidated into a Cedar policy string).

SetActiveBody.description:
Flip only `active` (P5's list-row toggle). A dedicated endpoint rather
than routing a toggle through `PUT .../alerts/{id}`, which is a FULL
REPLACE requiring every field — building a toggle on top of it would mean
a read-modify-write that could clobber a concurrent edit to the rest of
the schedule.

SetDashboardCertification.description:
Body for `PUT /dashboards/{id}/certification`.

A SEPARATE endpoint from the dashboard PUT on purpose: certification is guarded by the
platform-scoped `dashboard:certify`, while editing is guarded by the workspace-scoped
`dashboard:manage`. Folding these fields into `UpdateDashboard` would let any editor certify
their own dashboard by saving it, which is the failure this feature exists to avoid.

details.description:
Free text explaining the certification. Ignored when `certified` is false — withdrawing
clears the note rather than leaving a stale justification attached.

SetDatasetCertification.description:
Body of the dataset / metric certification endpoints. Deliberately carries NO `certified_by`:
the certifier is the session, exactly as it is for dashboards. A client that could name the
certifier could forge provenance, which is the defect 0109 closes.

details.description:
Ignored when `certified` is false — withdrawing clears the note rather than leaving a
stale justification attached to an uncertified dataset.

SetFeatures.description:
The feature keys to change; any key this workspace's catalog entry already
has is left exactly as it is. This is a merge, not a full replacement,
despite arriving over `PUT`: `PUT` is still the right verb because the
operation is idempotent (sending the same body twice yields the same
state) — it is not required to mention every field of the resource. A
merge is also forward-safe: when a sixth module joins the catalog, a
caller that still only sends today's five keys leaves it untouched
instead of implicitly switching it on, which is what a true full
replacement (write/delete a row for every key, mentioned or not) would do.

features.description:
Feature key -> enabled. Unknown keys are rejected with 400 and nothing
is written (`WorkspaceRepo::set_features` validates the whole batch
before opening its transaction). The *resulting* state — this batch
merged onto what is already stored — is also validated against
cross-module dependencies (currently: `dashboards` requires `charts`),
so a body that never mentions `dashboards` can still be rejected if it
would leave `dashboards` on and `charts` off.

folder_id.description: `null` moves the schedule back to Uncategorized.

SetNotebookWarehouse.description:
Request body for PUT /ws/{workspace}/notebook-settings/warehouse: choose the
notebook scratch warehouse + (optionally) the private namespace path. A
missing/empty `namespace` defaults to `["notebook"]`.

SetWorkspacesBody.description:
`PUT /engines/{id}/workspaces` body: the FULL desired set of workspace ids the
engine should be assigned to (the handler diffs it against the current set).

token.description:
Three-way, like SMTP's password: absent keeps the stored token, `""` is
rejected (a config with no token cannot deliver, so there is nothing
sensible to store), a value replaces it. Required on first write.

SlackConfigDto.description:
What a client may see. There is no token field — not a redacted one, an
ABSENT one, so no future serializer can start including it by accident.

has_token.description:
Always true when a row exists: `token_secret_id` is NOT NULL. It is
reported anyway so the editor's "a token is stored" line reads the same
field on both credential paths — see `redact_recipient_config`.

password.description:
Omitted means "keep the stored password"; `""` means "remove it".

Without the distinction, an editor that renders a blank field (because
it cannot show the real one) would erase the password on every save.

SmtpConfigDto.description:
What a GET returns.

There is deliberately no password field — not even an empty or masked one.
`has_password` is what the editor needs (to show "configured" and to let the
user keep the existing one), and it is a boolean, so no serialization change
can turn it into the secret.

has_password.description: Whether a password is stored. The password itself is never returned.

to.description: Where to send the probe. Defaults to the configured from-address.

SnippetBody.description: Create/update body for a SQL snippet.

StarRocksConfigBody.description:
Wire shape for `CreateEngineBody.starrocks`: FE/CN image + replicas +
optional per-role resources. Mirrors the `resources{cpuRequest,cpuLimit,
memRequest,memLimit}` shape [`parse_resources`] already understands.

delegationMode.description:
Opt into per-user delegation (Access parity slice 3): `"jwt"` |
`"impersonate"` | omitted/`None` (no delegation — the slice-2 open
engine default). The OIDC coordinates (jwks/issuer) and the
impersonation service-user credential are NOT accepted here — they're
derived from egret's own OIDC config / minted server-side (see
[`create_starrocks_engine`]), same posture as Trino's
`trinoConfig.auth.jwt` vs the delegator secret.

tlsEnabled.description:
Enable FE SSL on the MySQL-protocol port (:9030) when delegation is
configured. Defaults to `true` when `delegation_mode` is set; ignored
otherwise. `false` opts out of TLS while still enabling delegation
(e.g. a dev cluster where the extra listener setup isn't wanted).

feConfig.description:
FE (`fe.conf`) override keys → merged over egret's managed base by the
orchestrator. egret-managed keys ([`egret_engine_mgmt_api::SR_PROTECTED_FE_KEYS`])
are rejected up front by [`validate_sr_fe_config`]. Omitted ⇒ preserved on update.

cnConfig.description:
CN (`cn.conf`) override keys → rendered into a ConfigMap by the orchestrator.
Omitted ⇒ preserved on update.

cnAutoscaling.description:
CN horizontal autoscaling `{ minReplicas?, maxReplicas, targetCpuPercent? }`.
Stored/read as opaque JSON here; typed into `CnAutoscaling` at provision-req
assembly. Omitted ⇒ preserved on update.

pod.description:
Pod- & container-level scheduling / customization surface (nodeSelector,
tolerations, affinity, sidecars, …). Opaque JSON here; typed into
`StarRocksPod` at provision-req assembly. Omitted ⇒ preserved on update.

password.description: Required for a local-auth admin (step-up). OIDC admins re-auth via OIDC (Task 8).
Required for a local-auth caller (step-up). OIDC callers re-auth via OIDC.

StorageDto.description: Response DTO for a storage connection.

StorageInput.description:
Request body for creating/updating a global storage connection. A `new_secret`
takes precedence over a provided `secret_ref`: it mints a new global named
secret and binds the connection to it.

oneOf.description: Mint a new global named secret inline and use it as `secret_ref`.

params.description:
Template parameters substituted into `{{name}}` placeholders before the
query is sent to the engine.

TabularResult.description:
A fully-collected, in-memory query result (bounded by the caller's row limit).

`Serialize`/`Deserialize` are for the E4b contract crate + BI forwarding this
result directly across the seam boundary; today the store persists `columns`
and `rows` individually, so the whole-struct codecs are not yet exercised.

rows.description: Row-major cell values; each inner vec is one row aligned to `columns`.

TagDto.description:
A classification tag carried by an object (Access P3.1). Local snake_case DTO
so egret-bi does not depend on egret-controlplane. `assignment_count` is the
tag's global assignment count (as computed by `TagRepo`).

TestInput.description: Body for testing an unsaved connection (no `name`).

TlsMode.description:
How the connection is secured. Spelled out rather than inferred from the
port: 587-means-STARTTLS is a convention, not a rule, and guessing wrong
silently sends credentials in the clear.

UpdateCatalogBody.description:
`PUT /engines/{id}/catalogs/{cid}` body: replaces the stored `config` +
`secret_ref` in full (not a partial patch).

semantic_type.description: Semantic role driving smart rendering and chart defaults; "" = none. Rejected with 400 if not one of the listed values.

UpdateDashboard.description:
The dashboard PUT body — and, byte for byte, one stored revision (migration 0107).
`Serialize` is derived alongside `Deserialize` so the snapshot is produced from this exact
type rather than hand-built JSON that could drift from it; a compile error is how a new field
announces that revisions must carry it too.

UpdateEndpointInput.description:
The `PATCH` body: every field absent means "leave it alone".

`folder_id` and `source_ref` are nullable columns, so "absent" and "set to
null" are different requests and a plain `Option<Uuid>` cannot tell them
apart — an author moving an endpoint back to the root would silently get "no
change". They use [`double_option`], where absent is `None` and an explicit
`null` is `Some(None)`.

`state` and `live_version_id` are NOT here. They are the publish lifecycle,
and a draft edit must never be able to put an endpoint live or repoint what a
live one serves.
`deny_unknown_fields` for the same reason as [`CreateEndpointInput`]: on a
PATCH the failure mode is worse, because a typo'd key looks exactly like
"leave it alone" and the author sees the OLD value persist rather than a
zeroed one.

UpdateSchedule.description:
Update body. Same shape as create minus `type`, which is immutable: an alert
and a report have disjoint required fields, so flipping the type of an
existing row can only produce a row that violates its own constraints.

message.description:
A user-authored note carried into the notification body. Distinct from
`description`, which is the line the LIST shows.

message_footer.description:
The closing note, rendered UNDER the result — `message` opens the
notification, this one closes it, and an inline image sits between them.
Defaulted, so a client written before 0116 keeps working unchanged.

skip_if_empty.description: Metabase's `skip_if_empty`: send nothing when the run produced no rows.

targets.description:
Objects a REPORT delivers, in page order. Empty falls back to the
single `chart_id`/`dashboard_id`, which is every pre-0115 row.

UpdateSecretInput.description:
Request body for updating a global named secret. Any subset may be present:
a `name` triggers a rename (re-describing with `description`); a `type`+`data`
(or legacy `value`) rotates the underlying vault row.

UserRef.description: A minimal user reference (id + email) for the impersonation state on `/me`.

ValidatorType.description: How an alert's query result becomes a fire/don't-fire decision.

WhoCanAccess.description:
Reverse of `EffectiveAccess`: for one object, every principal who can reach it
and why (`who_can_access`). Mirror of the principal→access resolver.

features.description:
Module keys this workspace currently has switched on. Populated
wherever a caller reads a workspace's entitlements back (`list_ws`,
`get_ws`, `/api/me/workspaces`) via [`dto_with_features`]; left empty
by the create/lifecycle handlers, which echo the resource they just
mutated rather than reading entitlement state.

WorkspaceEngineDto.description: An engine assigned to a workspace (workspace-admin `…/engines` list payload).

WsEngineCatalogDto.description:
One catalog of an assigned engine, with the storage/secret NAME it maps to.
`storage_name`/`secret_name` are best-effort (`null` when unresolvable); the
secret VALUE is never exposed.

WsEngineDetailDto.description:
Read-only detail of an assigned engine: its catalogs, each resolved to the
storage connection (via the engine's warehouse) and secret name it uses.

WsEngineListDto.description: One egret-provisioned engine assigned to the workspace (list view).

data_api_bearer.description: A `data-api` audience JWT from `POST /oauth/token` (OAuth2 client_credentials). TTL 600s.
